narrative.overview:
The pass is the counter between the kitchen and the dining room, where every plate is checked before it goes out. The site is laid out like one: a clean, lit counter (the warm-paper ground) with the work set down on it to be inspected. The work is the product itself, shown in its own screenshots, its own stage names and its own documentation, and the site's job is to present it plainly enough that a lead can check it and sign off.

The system is the same one the board app uses, so the site and the product read as one object. It is flat and border-defined: surfaces are white panels with a 1px warm-grey edge, nothing is raised by a shadow, and a single enamel blue marks what can be acted on. Density is that of good documentation: generous line height, a 640–780px reading measure, small uppercase labels that name each section before its heading. Light and dark are both first-class; the dark palette is a chosen set of warm near-blacks, not an inversion.

The kitchen appears in the words and the mark (a pleated toque) and may appear visually only in sparing, restrained nods that earn their place. The site must never become a dark hacker hero: no black-first terminal aesthetic, no neon, no animated code.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, white bordered surfaces, no shadows.
One accent, enamel blue, for actions, links, the mark and the current page.
Figtree for everything readable, JetBrains Mono for keys, paths and code.
Product screenshots, in light and dark pairs, carry the visual weight.
Quiet and exact: thin borders, flat fills, precise spacing.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Enamel blue is the only hue on the site's own surfaces. Colour beyond it arrives only inside product screenshots.

rules.name: The Reserved Amber Rule
rules.body: The stylesheet carries the app's amber "Needs you" tokens so the two systems stay in step, but the site does not use them. Amber means a person is needed on a card; it never decorates a page.

rules.name: The Label-Then-Heading Rule
rules.body: A home-page section opens with an uppercase 11px label naming its category, then its heading. The label orients; the heading says something.

rules.name: The Flat Counter Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are separated by borders and tone, never by shadow or blur. If something needs to stand out, give it the accent, not height.

dos: Do take every colour from the custom properties in `site/src/site.css`, and keep them identical to the board app's tokens.
Do separate surfaces with a 1px Border and a tonal step; keep everything flat.
Do show the product with its own screenshots, always as a light and dark pair, framed like a card.
Do open home-page sections with an 11px uppercase label before the heading.
Do set keys, paths, commands and versions in JetBrains Mono.
Do design both themes at once; dark is a warm near-black palette, not an inversion.
Do keep any kitchen imagery to a sparing, restrained nod that earns its place; the toque mark is the anchor.
donts: Don't add shadows, glows or blur to lift a surface.
Don't introduce a second accent hue, and don't use the amber "Needs you" colour for decoration.
Don't turn the site into a dark hacker hero: no black-first terminal aesthetic, no neon green, no animated code.
Don't use emoji or exclamation marks, in copy or as icons.
